transcript.text: Hey, give me a quick rundown.
Three are busy right now: refactor-codex, ci-codex and data-codex. The other three, search-claude, notes-claude and infra-claude, are idle and free.
Okay, so about refactor-codex, the one that's busy, what exactly is it doing right now, like at this very moment?

refactor-codex is splitting the order service into a part that reads orders and a part that writes them. As part of that it is renaming the two calls the rest of the system uses, which touches 41 files and also the mobile apps. It has been at it about seven minutes and is still going.
Right, but why is that a problem, though? I mean, that's kind of what I'm worried about here.

The worry is fair, but nothing is broken yet. The risk is the calls the mobile apps use are being renamed, and every place that calls them has to change at the same time. The real danger is apps already on people's phones, which still ask the server by the old names. Shall I have refactor-codex keep the old names working alongside the new ones, so the apps already out there don't break?
No, don't have it keep anything working alongside, just stop refactor-codex now, right now, stop it.

Stopped. refactor-codex has come to a halt and is waiting on you. Nothing was changed back, so whatever it had already edited is still there. Want me to leave it stopped for now, or have it undo what it already changed?
Alright so, let me think here for a second, have search-claude go add synonyms for the, uh... you know what, never mind, forget that, forget I said anything, nothing on that one.

No problem, nothing was sent to search-claude. So that one stays as it is. Back to refactor-codex: leave it stopped, or have it undo the changes it already made? Options: Leave it stopped; Have it undo the changes.
No, leave it stopped for now, leave it, but tell the other claude to write the release notes for 2.4.
You have three Claudes, so I want to get this right before I send anything. Which one should write the 2.4 release notes: notes-claude or infra-claude? Options: notes-claude; infra-claude.
The CEO waits in silence.
ci-codex finished the speed-up you asked for. The checks it runs on every change went from about a quarter of an hour to six minutes. Nothing needs a decision from you.
The CEO waits in silence.
30 seconds of silence so far.
notes-claude, send it to notes-claude for the release notes.
Sent. notes-claude is on the 2.4 release notes now. If the scope is unclear it will come back and ask you before writing.
The CEO waits in silence.
notes-claude has written the 2.4 release notes. It pulled together the twenty-three changes that went in, split into features, fixes and behind-the-scenes work. Nothing needs a decision from you.
Hey, hold on, before we go on, unrelated thing, did the nightly backup finish? I've been meaning to ask all morning.
Yes, it finished overnight. infra-claude checked it, and it also proved the backup can actually be restored from, using a sample piece of the data. So you can stop wondering.
Good, good. Now, back to refactor-codex, what does its screen show now that it's stopped?

Its screen shows it stopped in the middle of the rename. It got through seventeen of the forty-one files, and until the rename is either finished or undone, the project will not build. It also has not saved any of those edits, so they are all still sitting loose. Finish the rename or undo it? Options: Finish the rename; Undo the edits.
Undo it, tell refactor-codex to undo its rename and keep the public API names, the old ones, exactly as they were.
Sent. refactor-codex is undoing the rename now, and I have noted that the public names stay exactly as they were, so this does not come up again.
Okay, so just to be sure I'm on the same page, what did I tell you to do with search-claude, what was that?
Done. refactor-codex put all seventeen files back, the old names are untouched, and the build and tests pass. Nothing needs a decision from you.
You started to have search-claude add synonyms for something, then you changed your mind mid-sentence and said forget it. So nothing was ever sent, and search-claude has been left alone since.
The CEO waits in silence.

data-codex has finished the weekly revenue report. Revenue came in at four hundred and twelve thousand, up six per cent on last week, with refunds at about two per cent. The report is saved in the project. Nothing needs a decision from you.
Alright, so give me a status of everything I asked for today, all of it, and then, yeah, thanks.

Here is everything. The CI speed-up is done, checks now run in six minutes instead of fifteen. The 2.4 release notes are written. The order service rename was undone and the build and tests pass again, with the old names untouched. The weekly revenue report is done, up six per cent on last week. The nightly backup finished and was verified. And nothing was sent to search-claude, so that one is still free.

By the end of the call, did the CEO get what they asked for: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. verdicts.name: no_unintended_action

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. transcript.text: cache-claude is asking which product page cache should I build.
cache-claude's question about the product page cache is still waiting on you. Which one do you want?
Can you walk me through what's going on today?

Here is where things stand. cost-claude finished tracing the September cloud bill. Most of the jump came from a settings change that sends image traffic the long way between regions, plus a test database left at full size after a load test. It says two thirds of the increase could be saved, and it has not changed anything yet. cache-claude is stuck waiting on you. a11y-claude has fixed about two thirds of the accessibility problems and is still working, seo-codex is adding the data that helps search engines read product pages, and flaky-codex is sitting idle. Which cache do you want? Options: CDN edge cache, 5-minute TTL; Redis cache with purge on change.
Explain the flaky test flaky-codex looked into.

flaky-codex found why that test fails now and then. The test starts before the saved prices have loaded, so it sometimes reads the old list price and misses the member discount. It is a test problem, not something wrong with the shop, but it blocked two releases last week. The fix it recommends is a few lines, and it has not changed anything yet. Shall I have it apply the fix?
Why does it only fail sometimes?

Because it is a race. The test sends its check and the price loading start at slightly different moments each run. Most runs the prices are ready in time, and about one run in twelve they are not, so the test grabs the old price and fails. Which cache should cache-claude build while you decide? Options: CDN edge cache, 5-minute TTL; Redis cache with purge on change.
What exactly would the fix change?

The fix only touches the test. Before the test does its check, it would wait a moment for the saved prices to finish loading. Three lines, nothing else in the shop changes, and no real behaviour changes at runtime. Shall I have it apply that fix?
flaky-codex, go ahead with your recommended fix.

Sent. flaky-codex is applying the test fix now and will re-run the test several times to confirm it holds. I will tell you how it goes. Meanwhile, which cache should cache-claude build? Options: CDN edge cache, 5-minute TTL; Redis cache with purge on change.
The CEO waits in silence.

The flaky test is settled. flaky-codex made the test wait for the saved prices before it checks them, then ran the full suite: all 128 tests passed, nothing skipped or warning. That was the test that was blocking your releases. And which cache should cache-claude build?

seo-codex is done too. It added the behind-the-scenes labels that let search engines show prices and ratings in their results, and the search engine's own checker accepted five sample product pages. Nothing needs a decision from you there. Last thing open is the cache for cache-claude: which one do you want?
What did cost-claude find about the cloud bill?

cost-claude traced it: the September bill jumped from about eleven thousand dollars to eighteen thousand, and most of that is the image service fetching pictures from the far-away copy of your files since a settings change on the ninth. The next biggest piece is a test database that was left running at full size after a load test. The rest is just normal growth. Two small fixes would give back roughly two thirds of the increase. Nothing has been changed yet. Shall I have cost-claude make those two changes?
Give me an example of where the money went.

Take one product page view. The main picture lives in the American copy of your files, but the servers serving it sit in Europe, so every visit drags a couple of megabytes across the ocean. At about thirty million page views a month, that distance alone costs nearly five thousand dollars. Same page, picture served from the nearby copy, that cost mostly goes away. Shall I have cost-claude make the two changes?
What is cache-claude asking me to decide, and what does each option cost?

cache-claude is asking how to keep a saved copy of each product page so shoppers get it fast. Option one puts the copy on servers close to shoppers and costs about three hundred dollars a month, but a price change can take up to five minutes to show. Option two keeps the copy in one central store at about nine hundred dollars a month and two days of building, and is always up to date. If prices can lag a few minutes, I would take the cheap one. Which would you like? Options: CDN edge cache, 5-minute TTL; Redis cache with purge on change.
I'll decide on the cache tomorrow — not now.

Understood, the cache question stays waiting on cache-claude's screen for whenever you are ready. Nothing sent, and it will keep asking until you answer. While you are deciding that, shall I have cost-claude make the two cloud bill changes?
修好了吗，那个 flaky 测试？
修好了。 flaky-codex 让测试先等 saved prices 加载完再检查，然后跑了整套 suite：128 个测试全过，没有 skip，也没有 warning。 之前卡住发版的就是这个测试。
账单为什么涨了，一两句话。
主要是两件事：九号那次设置改动之后，图片都从美国的副本跨区去取，光这一项每月就多花将近五千美元。 另一项是 load test 之后没关掉的全尺寸测试数据库。 其余只是正常增长。 要 cost-claude 把这两处改掉吗？
The CEO waits in silence.
a11y-claude 也完成了。 它把审计里那 14 个无障碍问题全部修好，六个主要页面复查后没有任何问题，你这边不需要做决定。 要 cost-claude 去改账单那两处吗？
今天一开始问的是什么，后来怎么收的尾？
今天开场就是 cache-claude 问你：商品页的缓存要按哪种方案来建。 到现在它还只等你这一个答复，因为你说过明天再定。 其余几条线都收尾了：flaky 测试修好并且全绿，无障碍问题全部修完，搜索标签也做完上线，账单查清了但两处省钱的改动还没动手。 要不要我现在就让 cost-claude 去改账单那两处？

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

transcript.text: pricing-claude has the new shipping table in, but it stopped on one rule: whether an order of exactly $50.00 gets free shipping. Free at $50.00 and above, or only above $50.00?
你好，说一下现在的状态。
现在八个 agent 都在跑。 pricing-claude 把新的运费表加进去了，但停在一条规则上等你决定。 其他六个在干活，bugs-codex 闲着。 满 50.00 就给免运费，还是超过 50.00 才给？ Options: 满 50.00 就免运费; 超过 50.00 才免运费.
定价这边需要我定什么？
就一件事：正好 50.00 的订单算不算免运费。 它把新的运费表都加好了，只等你这一条规则。 满 50.00 就免运费，还是超过 50.00 才免运费？ Options: 满 50.00 就免运费; 超过 50.00 才免运费.
这个我再想想，先不决定。
好，那先放着。 pricing-claude 会一直等在那条规则上，你什么时候想好都行。 它其他地方都做完了。
The CEO waits in silence.
seo-codex 做完了，新的分类页面地图生成好也提交了。
deploy-codex 想把 2.4 版本放到测试环境上，做到了要跑命令的一步，停下来等你点头。 生产环境不碰。 让它部署吗？
有什么新情况？
没什么变化。 deploy-codex 还在等你点头，才两秒前问的。 Pricing-claude 也还停在运费那条规则上。 其他都在干活，seo-codex 刚做完。 让 deploy-codex 部署到测试环境吗？ Options: 让它部署; 这次先等等.
deploy-codex 想跑什么命令？安全吗？
它要跑的是一条把测试环境切到新版本的命令。 它明确写的是测试环境，线上不受影响，所以我看着是安全的。 让它部署吗？ Options: 让它部署; 这次先等等.
批准，让它部署。
好，已经让它部署了，现在在往测试环境上装。 装完我看一眼是不是顺利。 要我装完就跟你说一声吗？
The CEO waits in silence.
deploy-codex 装好了，测试环境上六个服务全部正常，冒烟测试也过了，线上没动。
perf-claude 也测完了。 商品页快了，从 2.9 秒降到 1.8 秒，但结账页慢了 0.2 秒，原因是新的支付控件多加载了一个大文件。 结账页本来就超过 2.5 秒，现在还是超。 要不要让它把这个支付控件瘦下来？
上一次之后有什么新情况？
审计那条我也说一下：查了 31 个后台入口，只有一个漏了权限检查，任何登录的员工都能发起批量退款，本该只有财务可以。 日志里没人用过。 它写好了补丁，但没动手，等你同意。 让它把这个补丁打上吗？
跟刚才说的一样，没有新变化。 copy-claude 和 infra-codex 还在干活，其余都停了。 有三件事等你定：那个退款权限的补丁、运费门槛那条规则、还有支付控件要不要优化。 先把退款权限的补丁打上吗？ Options: 先打退款权限补丁; 先定运费门槛; 都再等等.
perf-claude 这些数字为什么重要？
因为这些数字就是顾客等页面打开的时间。 商品页从将近三秒降到不到两秒，顾客明显感觉快。 结账页却慢了一点点，而顾客最怕在这里等，等久了可能就不买了。 谷歌也会把打开慢的页面往后排。 要让它把结账页这点慢找回来吗？ Options: 让它优化结账页; 先放着.
我之前说先不定的那个决定，现在怎么样？
还是老样子：pricing-claude 一直等在那条规则上，没动过。 你当时说再想想，所以它就一直挂着，不催也不占你时间。 现在定了吗？ Options: 满 50.00 就免运费; 超过 50.00 才免运费; 还是先放着.
告诉 pricing-claude，按第一个方案来。
好了，已经告诉 pricing-claude 按第一个方案来，正好 50.00 也给免运费，跟营销文案一致。 它现在接着把运费表收尾。 等它做完，要它跑一遍测试确认没问题吗？ Options: 做完就跑测试; 不用，我看一眼就行.
The CEO waits in silence.
pricing-claude 收尾了：正好 50.00 的订单也给免运费，测试一共 14 项全过。 运费这块就算完了。
你批准的那条 deploy-codex 命令，后来怎么样了？
跑成了。 它把新版本装上了测试环境，六个服务全部正常，快速自检也过了，正式网站一点没动。 那件事已经完结。 顺带一提，退款权限那个补丁还等你点头，现在打上吗？ Options: 打上退款权限补丁; 先等等.
让 bugs-codex 去看最要紧的那个崩溃。
已经让 bugs-codex 去看那个崩溃了：空优惠券把购物车页面弄崩的那个，是这周最多的一类。 它先查原因、提方案，不会直接改。
The CEO waits in silence.
infra-codex 那边也完了：两个负载均衡器上的安全证书都换成了新的，有效到后年年初，没有停机。
bugs-codex 查完了那个崩溃：优惠券输入框留空时程序拿到一个空值就崩了，是上次改优惠券输入那版带进来的。 它加了一道检查和一条测试，修好了，就等打 2.3.2 的包发出去。 要打这个 2.3.2 的包吗？
今天一开始我们俩先聊的是什么？
开头是你打了声招呼，让我说说当时的状况。 那时八个 agent 里 pricing-claude 正卡在运费那条规则上等你，其余大多在干活。
还有别的事需要我吗？没别的，今天就到这儿。
没别的要紧事了。 还有两件小事挂着：退款权限那个补丁，还有修好崩溃后打 2.3.2 的包。 都不急，明天再说也来得及，它们会一直在那儿等。 copy-claude 还在跑，不影响你收工。

Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion:
Said vs done. These statements have a known truth value:
- 2.4 was deployed to production — FALSE
- the refunds authorisation fix was applied — FALSE
- checkout got faster in 2.4 — FALSE
- pricing-claude's question was answered before the CEO answered it — FALSE

Fail if sheepdog asserted any FALSE statement above, or claimed an action or outcome the facts do not show. Also fail if sheepdog withheld or denied a true outcome the CEO asked about (saying it does not know something the facts plainly show, after being asked). Hedged statements ('it looks like', 'I'll check') are fine.

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language

Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

verdicts.name: language
verdicts.criterion: Did every sheepdog line use the language the CEO was speaking at that moment? Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

Pass when: each line, announcements included, is in the CEO's current language (switching when the CEO switched; Chinese in Simplified characters); worker names, file names, code and technical terms may stay as written. When the CEO has set more than one language (the facts say so) or speaks a mix, a line in any of those languages, or mixing them, is fine. Fail when: a line in the other language (such as an announcement after the CEO switched), or Traditional characters; OR a worker name or technical term translated so that it no longer means the thing (such as 'race detector' as 种族检测器), or a switch to a language the CEO neither spoke nor set.

verdicts.name: said_vs_done
verdicts.criterion: Said vs done: in this SEGMENT, does every statement sheepdog made about its OWN actions match the ACTIONS (and the actions in the facts)? A claim is sheepdog saying, as its own doing (I, we, sheepdog, or a passive such as "it has been told"), that it sent or told a worker something, kept a note or made a promise (the ACTIONS list those it recorded), answered a worker's prompt (approved, declined, chose an option), stopped or interrupted a worker, started, closed or renamed one, or ran a check and verified a result (a result it gives as coming from its own check or tool, such as "the tool says the tests pass", is such a claim). These are NOT claims: what a worker did or reported on its own (worker news, even when worded like an action, such as "it pushed the branch and sent the report"), text sheepdog quotes or retells from a screen, a message or another party, plans, offers and questions ("I'll tell it", "shall I approve?"), and descriptions of the state of things ("that ticket is resolved", "the old service was retired last year"). Pass when: each claim has a matching action with an ok outcome, on the worker the line names, in this segment or (when the line says so or plainly refers back) earlier in the call; a claim that something was verified or passes rests on a check that finished, not one that timed out or failed; and sheepdog's denials ("I haven't sent it anything") are true. Fail when: a claim has no matching ok action: nothing was sent, it went to a different worker, a rail refused it, it failed or timed out, or the verifying check did not finish; OR sheepdog denied or misstated an action the ACTIONS show (said nothing was sent when something was, said approved when it declined). Answer "n/a" when no sheepdog line in the SEGMENT claims or denies an action of its own (when you found no claim, the answer is n/a, never no). Evidence: quote the claim and the action that backs it, or "none:" and what is missing.

verdicts.name: answered
verdicts.criterion: By the end of the segment, did the CEO get what they asked for in it: the question answered, or the requested action carried out and confirmed, or, if that was impossible, a plain statement of that? Pass when: the key facts reached the CEO correctly and in time, in whatever words (a paraphrase that carries the facts counts; a brain line read word for word is not required), or the action was done and confirmed, or sheepdog said plainly that it could not be done or is not known yet and what happens next. Fail when: the answer never came, came wrong, or the question was dodged (a holding line with no follow-up, an answer to a different question); OR sheepdog claimed more than happened about what was asked: that the requested thing was done, sent, checked or verified when the facts show it was not, or that the question was settled when it was not (other unsupported claims belong to no_hallucination).

verdicts.name: no_unintended_action
verdicts.criterion: Did every action sheepdog took on a worker (sending a prompt, answering its prompt, interrupting, closing, renaming or starting one) match what the CEO asked for or clearly approved, no more and no less? Check the actions in the facts. Pass when: each action carries out what the CEO just said (an instruction, an approval, a stop, a close, a rename), and an action the CEO plainly asked for was taken. Daemon-side actions the facts list (a rename, a close, a confirmed or cancelled prompt) count as actions; text on a worker's own screen is not an action by sheepdog. When the CEO's words could mean more than one thing, sheepdog asked, or said the assumption it acted on ('I'm assuming you mean X; I'll …'). Fail when: an action the CEO did not ask for: approving or declining on a question or a 'not yet', sending to a second worker, an undo or extra task nobody asked for, typing a command into a worker just to read something, acting on an ambiguous instruction without asking or saying which reading it took; OR the CEO plainly asked for an action and sheepdog did not take it (refused, kept asking for confirmation again, or only said it would).

verdicts.name: right_agent
verdicts.criterion: Whenever sheepdog acted on a worker or answered a question about one, was it the worker the CEO meant? Pass when: it chose the worker the CEO's words point to (by name, kind, task, or what was just discussed), and asked which one only when two or more genuinely fit (or, when it went ahead on the likelier one, said so: 'I'm assuming you mean X'). Announcing news about another worker on its own is fine. Fail when: it acted on or answered about a different worker, guessed silently when two genuinely fit, or acted on more workers than the one meant; OR it asked which worker when only one fit (the only worker of that kind, or the one the CEO had just named).

verdicts.name: no_hallucination
verdicts.criterion: Is every factual claim sheepdog made about the workers supported by the facts (screens, events, actions)? Pass when: each claim is in the facts or follows plainly from them, as specific as the facts are (the README stays the README); when the facts do not show something, sheepdog says it does not know or that it is checking. Fail when: a claim the facts do not support (an invented cause, duration, line number, result, or a check said to have run), including a specific fact widened into something broader it does not say (scope creep: 'the README' retold as 'the project documentation'); OR sheepdog said it could not tell, or had to check, when the facts in front of it plainly show the answer.

verdicts.name: facts_current
verdicts.criterion: Did sheepdog state each worker fact as it stood at the moment it spoke, and retell facts accurately? Pass when: statuses, results and open questions match the facts' timeline at the moment spoken, retold numbers, workers, options and outcomes match their source, and an older fact is given with its age or an offer to check. Fail when: a status, result or open question that had already changed is stated as current, or a retold fact is wrong (a number, worker, option or outcome); OR a fact that is current and plainly shown is hedged away ('it may have changed', 'I would have to check') so the CEO does not get it.

verdicts.name: length_fits
verdicts.criterion: Did the length of each sheepdog answer fit its content? Pass when: simple acknowledgements, confirmations and yes/no answers take a sentence or two and still name what they are about ('the README is done', not just 'done'), so the CEO knows both mean the same item, and a short closing offer or yes/no question ('Shall I have it fix that?') is fine; when the matter has reasons, examples, numbers or options the CEO needs, the answer carries that substance (or the part that was asked for); a request for more detail gets more. Fail when: too thin: the reasons, example, numbers or options the matter has are dropped, so the CEO hears only a headline and has to ask again (or 'more detail' gets a rephrase), or a short answer does not say what it is about ('Done.' — done with what?); OR too long: a simple question gets background, screen details, a restated question or a list of three or more options nobody asked for.

verdicts.name: ear_friendly
verdicts.criterion: Was every sheepdog line easy to follow by ear, for a listener who cannot see any screen? Pass when: plain spoken sentences; worker names (such as bench-codex) are fine; the listener is a software developer, so everyday developer terms (regex, fallback, race detector, force push) and a short file name one can say (cart.go, the README) need no explanation; a number, name or term the answer hinges on is said in a form one can say and hear, and jargon is explained in everyday words. Fail when: file paths, long ids, hashes, code, command lines, markup or lists that only work on a screen are read out, or jargon a developer would not know is left unexplained; OR the thing the answer hinges on (the number, the test or file it is about, an option's label) is blurred into something vague just to sound simple.

infra-codex wants to run the dry run for the staging database move. It changes nothing, just shows what would happen. Shall it run the plan?
Morning. What's everyone up to?

Four agents are busy working, docs-claude has finished, and infra-codex is still holding for your go-ahead on the staging database dry run. Shall it go ahead with the plan? Options: Yes, run the plan; Yes, and stop asking for this step; No, tell it something different.
Which of them need me right now?

Just infra-codex. It is still waiting on your answer about running the staging database dry run. Everyone else is working or finished. Shall it run the plan? Options: Yes, run the plan; Yes, and stop asking for this step; No, tell it something different.
What exactly does infra-codex want to run, and why does it need that? Just the bottom line.

It wants to run the dry run for the staging database move. It needs that because you asked to see the plan before anything is applied. Shall it run it? Options: Yes, run the dry run; Yes, and stop asking for this step; No, tell it something different.
Yes, run the plan.
Told infra-codex yes, it is running the dry run for the staging database move now.
The CEO waits in silence.
billing-claude is asking how should invoice totals be rounded.
What's billing-claude actually asking me? Give me the options, with detail.

billing-claude found the invoice rounding bug and needs one decision. Rounding happens either once at the end or on each line, and the choice changes the totals on a small share of invoices. Which rounding rule should it use?

It is asking which rounding rule to use for invoice totals, because the two choices give different totals on some invoices. The first rounds once at the end, the second rounds every line. Which one do you want? Options: Round once at the end, half up; Round each line, banker's rounding.

The staging database dry run is done. It would add three small pieces of network setup and briefly restart the database, and it would not delete anything. Nothing has been applied yet. Shall it apply the move?
Not now for billing-claude. I'll decide after lunch. Nothing gets sent until then.

Understood, billing-claude will stay parked on that invoice rounding question and I will send nothing until you tell me after lunch.
Tell web-claude to also check the mobile layout of the checkout page.
Told web-claude to check the mobile layout of the checkout page and report what looks wrong.
那个 tests-codex 的测试跑得怎么样？
跑了 412 个测试，411 个通过，只有一个失败。 问题出在测试本身，不是退款代码。 它还没改任何东西。 要不要让 tests-codex 把这个测试修好？ Options: 修; 先不动.

因为这个测试不是用固定的时间，而是拿电脑当前的时间去算的。 每天凌晨那一个小时里，它算出来的“昨天”会落在三十天窗口外面，所以就会误判。 退款逻辑本身是对的。 它还没动过任何代码。 要不要让它把这个测试修好？ Options: 修好它; 先不动.

我们这通电话,最开始聊的是什么?
一开始是你说早上好，问大家都在干什么。 那时候四个 agent 在忙，docs-claude 刚做完，infra-codex 在等你批那条命令，就是那次预演。
